name: White Yam Tuber
desc: Large, premium white yam from the famous Ikole yam belt of Ekiti.

name: Water Yam (Ewura)
desc: Soft, moist water yam — great boiled, pounded or in porridge.

name: Yellow Yam
desc: Golden-fleshed yam with a rich taste, lovely for boiling and frying.

name: Sweet Potato
desc: Red-skinned sweet potatoes — naturally sweet.

name: Irish Potato
desc: Firm Irish potatoes for chips, porridge and stews.

name: Cocoyam (Taro)
desc: Starchy cocoyam corms, used for soups and pottage.

name: Fresh Cassava
desc: Freshly harvested cassava roots, ready for fufu or garri.

name: Beetroot
desc: Deep red, sweet beetroot for salads, juices and stews.
tip: Cut the leaves off, leave 2 cm of stem, and keep chilled for up to 3 weeks. Boil whole before peeling to keep the colour.

name: Radish (White)
desc: Crisp, peppery white radish, eaten raw or lightly cooked.
tip: Best fresh in salads. Keep in the fridge and use within a week.

name: Turnip
desc: Mild, slightly sweet turnips for soups, stews and roasting.
tip: Peel before cooking; keeps 2 weeks in a cool place.

name: Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potato
desc: Sweet, vitamin-A-rich orange sweet potato.
tip: Boil, roast or fry. Store cool, dark and dry; never in the fridge.

name: Purple Sweet Potato
desc: Purple-fleshed sweet potato with a rich, nutty sweetness.
tip: Steam or roast to keep the colour. Store cool and dark.

name: Puna Yam
desc: Firm, white Puna yam known for pounding smooth.
tip: Great for pounded yam and boiling. Keep in a ventilated, shaded place.

name: Yam Bean (Jicama)
desc: Crunchy, juicy, lightly sweet jicama root.
tip: Peel and eat raw in salads or with pepper. Keep chilled up to 2 weeks.

name: Sweet Cassava (Eating Variety)
desc: Low-bitterness cassava that can be boiled or fried.
tip: Cook within 2–3 days of purchase because cassava spoils fast.

name: Aerial Yam
desc: Small yam-like tubers that grow on the vine, good boiled or roasted.
tip: Peel, boil well and eat with stew or oil. Use within a week.

name: Sweet Maize (Corn)
desc: Fresh sweet corn on the cob, harvested this morning from the field.

name: Ofada Rice (Local Unpolished)
desc: Aromatic local ofada rice, stone-free and carefully sorted.

name: Local Long-Grain Rice
desc: Clean local parboiled long-grain rice for jollof and everyday meals.

name: Dry White Maize
desc: Clean, dry white maize grain for pap, milling and feed.
tip: Keep sealed and dry; milled maize makes ogi (pap) and tuwo.

name: Dry Yellow Maize
desc: Dry yellow maize for grits, milling and animal feed.
tip: Store in a dry, airy bag away from damp.

name: Popcorn Kernels
desc: Pop-ready kernels for a quick, crunchy snack.
tip: Heat in a covered pot with a little oil; keep kernels sealed so they stay poppable.

name: Red Guinea Corn (Sorghum)
desc: Red sorghum for pap, kunu and traditional brews.
tip: Wash, soak and mill for kunu or pap. Keep dry.

name: White Guinea Corn (Sorghum)
desc: White sorghum for tuwo, kunu and porridge.
tip: Pound or mill for tuwo. Keep dry and sealed.

name: Pearl Millet (Jero)
desc: Nutritious pearl millet for fura, tuwo and porridge.
tip: Wash well, then use for fura or tuwo. Store dry.

name: Acha (Fonio)
desc: Tiny, quick-cooking fonio grain, a premium traditional cereal.
tip: Steam like couscous in 10 minutes or cook as porridge. Rinse to remove grit.

name: Brown Rice (Whole Grain)
desc: Whole-grain brown rice, higher in fibre than white rice.
tip: Needs more water and about 40 minutes to cook. Keep sealed.

name: Local Rice (50kg Bag)
desc: Full 50 kg bag of clean local rice, ideal for homes, events and resale.
tip: Store raised off the floor in a dry room.

name: Wheat Grain
desc: Whole wheat grain for milling and baking.
tip: Mill into flour or boil whole for porridge. Keep dry.

name: Oats (Whole Grain)
desc: Whole oats for breakfast porridge and baking.
tip: Cook with milk or water for 5–10 minutes. Keep sealed.

name: Green Beans
desc: Crisp green beans for fried rice and stir-fry.

name: Brown Beans (Oloyin)
desc: Sweet, honey-type brown beans for ewa agoyin, moi moi and porridge.
tip: Pick out stones, soak, then boil. Keeps a year when dry and sealed.

name: White Beans (Ewa Funfun)
desc: Clean white beans for moi moi, akara and beans porridge.
tip: Soak and peel for smooth akara and moi moi.

name: Soybeans
desc: Protein-rich soybeans for soy milk, flour and cooking.
tip: Boil thoroughly; never eat raw. Great for soy milk and daddawa.

name: Groundnut (Shelled)
desc: Clean shelled groundnuts for roasting, groundnut oil and sauces.
tip: Roast, boil or grind. Store cool and dry to prevent mould.

name: Groundnut (In Shell)
desc: Groundnuts in the shell, fresh and ready to boil or roast.
tip: Boil in the shell with salt or roast. Keep dry.

name: Bambara Nut
desc: Traditional bambara groundnut for okpa and porridge.
tip: Soak overnight and cook long, or mill for okpa.

name: Pigeon Pea (Fiofio)
desc: Fiofio pigeon peas for porridge, stews and soups.
tip: Soak, then simmer until soft. Keep dry.

name: African Yam Bean (Sese)
desc: Rare, protein-rich African yam bean for traditional dishes.
tip: Needs long soaking and slow cooking.

name: Egusi (Melon Seeds)
desc: Shelled egusi seeds for the classic Nigerian soup.
tip: Grind and fry in oil for egusi soup. Keep cool and dry.

name: Beniseed (Sesame)
desc: Clean sesame seeds for toasting, oil and sauces.
tip: Toast lightly and use on bread, in sauces or for oil. Store cool.

name: Sunflower Seeds
desc: Raw sunflower seeds for snacking and oil.
tip: Roast lightly for snacking. Keep sealed and cool.

name: Tiger Nut
desc: Sweet, chewy tiger nuts — snack or make kunun aya.

name: Pineapple
desc: Sweet, juicy farm pineapple.
tip: Ripe when fragrant at the base. Eat within 3–4 days or chill cut fruit.

name: Watermelon
desc: Large, sweet watermelon, great for hot days.
tip: Chill before cutting. A ripe one sounds hollow when tapped.

name: Sweet Oranges
desc: Juicy sweet oranges for eating and juice.
tip: Keep cool; they last about a week, longer in the fridge.

name: Bananas
desc: Sweet bananas sold by the bunch.
tip: Ripen at room temperature; keep away from other fruit if you want them slower.

name: Unripe Plantain
desc: Firm green plantains for boiling, chips and porridge.
tip: Keep at room temperature; use within a week or let it ripen.

name: Ripe Plantain
desc: Soft, yellow plantains for dodo (fried plantain) and roasting (boli).
tip: Use within 2–3 days; peel and freeze extras for dodo.

name: Pawpaw (Papaya)
desc: Sweet, soft pawpaw rich in vitamins.
tip: Ripe when the skin yellows and gives slightly. Chill and eat within 3 days.

name: Mango
desc: Sweet, juicy seasonal mangoes.
tip: Ripen at room temperature, then refrigerate.

name: Avocado Pear
desc: Creamy avocado pears for eating, salads and smoothies.
tip: Ripe when it gives under gentle pressure. Keep cut halves with the stone.

name: Coconut
desc: Fresh coconuts with sweet water and firm flesh.
tip: Drink the water first, then eat or grate the flesh for rice and snacks.

name: Cashew Nuts (Raw, Shelled)
desc: Shelled raw cashew nuts, a premium snack and cooking nut.
tip: Roast lightly before eating. Keep sealed in a cool place.

name: Kola Nut
desc: Traditional kola nuts for ceremonies and chewing.
tip: Keep damp in a leaf or cloth so it stays fresh.

name: Ripe Tomatoes
desc: Plump, vine-ripened tomatoes. Perfect for stews, sauces and soups.

name: Farm Pumpkin
desc: Large, fresh pumpkin — ideal for porridge, soups and seeds.

name: Green Cucumbers
desc: Crisp, field-grown cucumbers — great fresh, in salads, or juiced.

name: Fluted Pumpkin Leaf (Ugu)
desc: Fresh ugu leaves for efo riro, egusi and vegetable soup.

name: Efo Tete (Green Amaranth)
desc: Tender green amaranth leaves, a Yoruba soup staple.

name: Efo Shoko (Celosia)
desc: Soft celosia leaves, lovely cooked in stew or with palm oil.

name: Ewedu (Jute Leaf)
desc: Fresh jute leaves for smooth, slippery ewedu soup.

name: Waterleaf
desc: Juicy waterleaf for edikang ikong, afang and everyday soups.

name: Bitter Leaf
desc: Washed, ready-to-use bitter leaf for ofe onugbu and soups.

name: Okra
desc: Young, tender okra pods — perfect for draw soup.

name: Garden Egg
desc: Fresh garden eggs, eaten raw with groundnut or cooked in sauces.

name: Onions
desc: Firm, well-cured onions for everyday cooking.

name: Carrots
desc: Sweet, crunchy carrots for salads, rice and juice.

name: Cabbage
desc: Fresh, tight green cabbage heads for salads and stir-fry.

name: Lettuce
desc: Crunchy lettuce heads for salads and sandwiches.

name: Spinach
desc: Fresh spinach leaves, perfect for soups and smoothies.

name: Oha Leaf
desc: Tender oha leaves for the famous oha soup.
tip: Tear (do not cut) and add late in cooking. Use within 2 days.

name: Afang Leaf (Okazi)
desc: Shredded-ready afang leaf for afang soup.
tip: Slice very thin, pound or blend, and cook with waterleaf. Use within 2 days.

name: Cauliflower
desc: Firm, white cauliflower heads.
tip: Steam, roast or stir-fry. Keep chilled up to a week.

name: Broccoli
desc: Fresh green broccoli for stir-fries and rice.
tip: Steam lightly to keep the colour. Use within 4–5 days.

name: Green Bell Pepper
desc: Crisp green bell peppers for fried rice, salads and sauces.
tip: Keep dry in the fridge up to 10 days.

name: Spring Onions
desc: Fresh spring onions for garnish, fried rice and stir-fry.
tip: Wrap in a damp cloth in the fridge; use within a week.

name: Celery
desc: Crisp celery stalks for soups, salads and rice dishes.
tip: Keep upright in water in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

name: Fresh Pepper (Tatashe & Rodo Mix)
desc: Freshly harvested Tatashe and Rodo pepper blend, sorted and ready for stews.

name: Ata Rodo (Scotch Bonnet)
desc: Fiery, fruity scotch bonnet — the classic Nigerian hot pepper.

name: Tatashe (Red Bell Pepper)
desc: Large, mild red peppers that give stews their deep colour.

name: Shombo (Long Cayenne Pepper)
desc: Long, medium-hot cayenne pepper, great fresh or dried.

name: Ata Wewe (Small Hot Chilli)
desc: Tiny, very hot chillies for pepper soup and sauces.

name: Cameroon Pepper (Ata Ijosi)
desc: Small, aromatic and very hot — a favourite for dry pepper.

name: Scent Leaf (Efirin)
desc: Aromatic scent leaf for pepper soup and stews.

name: Fresh Ginger
desc: Spicy fresh ginger roots for tea, cooking and drinks.

name: Fresh Turmeric
desc: Fresh turmeric roots for cooking, tea and wellness drinks.

name: Garlic
desc: Firm, aromatic garlic bulbs.
tip: Store dry and airy for months; crush fresh for the best flavour.

name: Uziza Leaf
desc: Peppery uziza leaves for soups and pepper soup.
tip: Slice fine and add near the end. Use within 3 days or dry.

name: Uziza Seeds
desc: Dried uziza seeds, a hot, aromatic seasoning.
tip: Grind and use sparingly in pepper soup and stews. Keep sealed.

name: Utazi Leaf
desc: Bitter-sweet utazi leaf for soups and traditional dishes.
tip: Wash and slice fine; a little goes a long way.

name: Lemongrass (Fresh)
desc: Fragrant lemongrass stalks for tea and soups.
tip: Boil as tea or add to soups. Freezes well.

name: Cloves (Dried)
desc: Whole dried cloves, a strong aromatic spice.
tip: Use one or two per pot; keep sealed away from light.

name: Calabash Nutmeg (Ehuru)
desc: Ehuru, the fragrant calabash nutmeg used in pepper soup.
tip: Toast, crack and grind just before using.

name: Alligator Pepper (Atare)
desc: Atare seeds used in traditional ceremonies and spice blends.
tip: Crush the seeds and use in small amounts.

name: Grains of Selim (Uda)
desc: Smoky, aromatic uda pods for pepper soup and stews.
tip: Toast and crush before use; keep sealed.

name: Thyme (Dried)
desc: Dried thyme for stews, jollof and meat.
tip: Add early to stews. Keep in an airtight jar.

name: Bay Leaves (Dried)
desc: Dried bay leaves for rice, stews and soups.
tip: Add whole and remove before serving.

name: Black Pepper (Peppercorns)
desc: Whole black peppercorns with a sharp, warm bite.
tip: Grind fresh for the best flavour; keep sealed.

name: Garri (White)
desc: Crisp, well-fried white garri — fine, clean and sour-free.

name: Garri (Yellow)
desc: Palm-oil yellow garri with a rich colour and taste.

name: Cassava Flour (Lafun)
desc: Smooth, fine lafun for a soft, stretchy amala.

name: Fufu Flour
desc: Quick-mix cassava fufu flour — just add hot water.

name: Red Palm Oil (1 Litre)
desc: Pure, unbleached red palm oil for stews, banga and ofada sauce.
tip: Keep sealed away from heat. It may solidify in cool weather; warm gently to pour.

name: Groundnut Oil (1 Litre)
desc: Golden groundnut oil for frying and cooking.
tip: Good for frying at high heat. Store in a cool, dark place.

name: Yam Flour (Elubo)
desc: Dried yam flour for smooth amala isu.
tip: Stir into boiling water for amala; keep sealed and dry.

name: Plantain Flour
desc: Unripe plantain flour for a soft, healthy swallow.
tip: Stir into hot water like amala. Keep dry.

name: Tapioca
desc: Dried tapioca pearls for pudding and sweet desserts.
tip: Soak and boil until clear. Keep dry.

name: Locust Beans (Iru)
desc: Fermented locust beans, the savoury seasoning for soups and stews.
tip: Keep refrigerated or frozen; add to soup after the oil is hot.

name: Ogbono (Dried Seeds)
desc: Dried ogbono (wild mango) seeds for draw soup.
tip: Grind and stir into hot palm oil for ogbono soup. Keep sealed.

name: Kuli-Kuli (Groundnut Cake)
desc: Crunchy kuli-kuli, a classic groundnut snack.
tip: Eat with garri and sugar or on its own. Keep dry and sealed.

name: Wara (Local Cheese)
desc: Soft, fresh Nigerian cheese made from cow milk.
tip: Keep in water in the fridge and eat within 3–4 days.

name: Large White Pig (Live)
desc: Fast-growing Large White breed, vet-checked. Sold live by weight.

name: Landrace Pig (Live)
desc: Long-bodied Landrace breed, good meat yield. Sold live by weight.

name: Duroc Pig (Live)
desc: Hardy red Duroc breed with well-marbled meat. Sold live by weight.

name: Fresh Pork (Dressed)
desc: Cleaned, dressed pork sold by the kilo, ready for the kitchen.

name: Weaner Pig
desc: Recently weaned pig, active and feeding well — ready to grow out on your farm.

name: White Fulani (Bunaji) Cattle
desc: Gentle, dual-purpose White Fulani — good for milk and beef.

name: Red Bororo (Rahaji) Cattle
desc: Hardy, long-horned Red Bororo — strong and heat-tolerant.

name: Sokoto Gudali Cattle
desc: Large, muscular Sokoto Gudali — a top beef breed.

name: Goat (Live)
desc: Healthy West African Dwarf goats, good for meat and breeding.
tip: Keep in a clean, dry pen with water. Comes with a vet health certificate.

name: Yankasa Sheep (Live)
desc: Hardy Yankasa sheep, a popular meat breed.
tip: Provide shade and clean water on arrival. Comes with a vet health certificate.

name: Sallah Ram (Large)
desc: Large, well-fed rams, popular for festivals and ceremonies.
tip: Order early before festivals. Comes with a vet health certificate.

name: Rabbit (Live)
desc: Healthy rabbits for meat or breeding.
tip: Keep cool, dry and shaded; feed greens and pellets.

name: Fresh Beef
desc: Freshly butchered beef cuts, hygienically packed.
tip: Refrigerate and cook within 2 days, or freeze in portions.

name: Goat Meat (Fresh)
desc: Fresh goat meat for pepper soup, suya and stews.
tip: Refrigerate and cook within 2 days, or freeze.

name: Raw Honey (1 Litre)
desc: Pure, unprocessed forest honey.
tip: Store sealed at room temperature; it may crystallise, which is natural.

name: Fresh Cow Milk
desc: Fresh farm cow milk, delivered chilled.
tip: Keep refrigerated and boil before drinking; use within 2 days.

name: Giant African Snails (Live)
desc: Large, live giant African land snails.
tip: Keep in a cool, damp, ventilated container and cook within a few days.

name: Fresh Eggs (Crate of 30)
desc: Farm-fresh table eggs, collected daily and sold by the crate of 30.

name: Table-Ready Broiler
desc: Vet-cleared broilers, sold live or dressed (processed) by the kilo.

name: Broiler Chicks (8wks)
desc: 8-week-old broiler chicks, vaccinated, ready for finishing to table weight.

name: Point-of-Lay Layer Hen
desc: Young laying hens about to start production.
tip: Provide layer mash, clean water and nesting boxes.

name: Local Free-Range Chicken (Live)
desc: Free-range local chicken with firm, flavourful meat.
tip: Ideal for pepper soup and traditional dishes.

name: Cockerel (Live)
desc: Healthy live cockerels for the pot or for rearing.
tip: Keep in a ventilated cage and cook or rear soon.

name: Turkey (Live)
desc: Well-fed live turkeys for festive occasions.
tip: Order early for festive seasons. Comes with a vet certificate.

name: Duck (Live)
desc: Healthy live ducks for meat and rearing.
tip: Provide clean water for drinking and a dry shelter.

name: Guinea Fowl (Live)
desc: Live guinea fowl, a lean, flavourful local bird.
tip: Keep in an enclosure with shade and water.

name: Quail Eggs (Tray of 30)
desc: Small, rich quail eggs sold by the tray of 30.
tip: Boil 3–4 minutes for snacks and salads. Keep cool.

name: Day-Old Chicks
desc: Vaccinated day-old chicks for starting your own flock.
tip: Provide warmth (brooder), clean water and starter feed immediately.

name: Chicken Parts (Drumsticks & Thighs)
desc: Cleaned, packed chicken drumsticks and thighs.
tip: Refrigerate and cook within 2 days, or freeze.

name: Live Catfish
desc: Live pond-raised catfish, sold by weight.
tip: Keep in water until cooking. Great for pepper soup and grilling.

name: Smoked Catfish
desc: Hot-smoked catfish for soups and stews.
tip: Wash briefly and add to soup. Keeps well when frozen.

name: Fresh Tilapia
desc: Fresh pond tilapia, cleaned on request.
tip: Cook the same day or freeze. Good grilled or in pepper soup.

name: Smoked Tilapia
desc: Smoked tilapia for soups and stews.
tip: Rinse and add near the end of cooking.

name: Frozen Titus (Mackerel)
desc: Frozen titus mackerel, a popular affordable fish.
tip: Thaw in the fridge and cook the same day.

name: Croaker Fish (Frozen)
desc: Frozen croaker fish for stews and frying.
tip: Thaw slowly in the fridge before cooking.

name: Stockfish (Okporoko)
desc: Dried stockfish for egusi, afang and ogbono soups.
tip: Soak in hot water until soft, then clean and cook.

name: Smoked Bonga Fish (Shawa)
desc: Smoky bonga fish for soups and stews.
tip: Rinse, debone and add to soup for flavour.

name: Dried Crayfish (Whole)
desc: Dried crayfish, the essential Nigerian soup flavour.
tip: Grind or use whole; keep sealed in a dry place.

name: Fresh Prawns
desc: Fresh prawns, cleaned and chilled.
tip: Cook quickly (3–4 minutes) to keep them tender.

name: Catfish Fingerlings
desc: Healthy catfish fingerlings for pond stocking, sold per fingerling, per pack of 100 or per pond lot.
tip: Acclimatise slowly to pond water before releasing.
